points.description: States that insertion and deletion operations in a doubly-linked list can be performed in constant time / O(1).
points.partial_credit: Half credit (1.5) if the answer says insertion/deletion are faster or easier but does not state constant time/O(1), or states constant time for only one of insertion or deletion.

levels.says: Says insertion/deletion are faster/easier or more efficient, or states constant time for only one of insertion or deletion, but does not state that both insertion and deletion are constant time/O(1).

points.description: Identifies that the constant-time advantage covers operations before a given location/node in the list (e.g., inserting or deleting before a specified node). Accept 'all positions' or 'any position' as covering this.
Identifies that the constant-time advantage covers operations at the end of the list (e.g., deleting the last node). Accept 'all positions', 'any position' or 'at the tail' as covering this.

rubric.notes: Full marks require the answer to state that insertion and deletion are constant time/O(1) and to explicitly cover operations before a given location and at the end. Award 1.5/3 on P1 for a vague 'faster/easier' claim or for constant time on only one operation; P2 and P3 are all-or-nothing. No marks for only saying a doubly-linked list can be traversed backwards or uses extra memory, as these do not state the constant-time insertion/deletion advantage.
